item.text:
**6B.3 Research Note: Narendra Modi (2024)**

**Bottom line**
The record is **mixed but somewhat positive on targeted welfare delivery**, especially for women, rural households, minority women, farmers, and some pension/protection categories. The strongest positive evidence is programmatic: expanded housing, SHG mobilization, minority scholarships/skills, health coverage, and fiscal support for disadvantaged groups. The strongest negative evidence is that these benefits sat alongside persistent rural distress, communal polarization, and severe failures in places like Manipur and Jammu and Kashmir. So Modi did prioritize vulnerable groups in many program lines, but the execution and political context weaken any clean affirmative.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Title:** Interim budget centered disadvantaged groups
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint
  - **Date:** 1 Feb 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-finance-minister-unveils-budget-with-focus-on-poor-women-youth-and-farmers/1948406/
  - **Claim summary:** Reuters reported that the budget explicitly prioritized the poor, women, youth, and farmers while avoiding a giveaway structure. This is the clearest early signal that the government was formally prioritizing vulnerable groups.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

- **Title:** Government resisted pre-election giveaway politics
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint
  - **Date:** 1 Feb 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/economy/india-refrains-from-populist-budget-before-election-trims-fiscal-deficit/1948823/
  - **Claim summary:** Reuters said the administration kept fiscal consolidation and avoided a classic pre-poll splurge. That supports a reading that social support was being routed through budgetary discipline rather than pure patronage.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 5B.10, 6B.2

- **Title:** Health access expanded through Ayushman Bharat, U-WIN, and new medical seats
  - **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
  - **Date:** 28 Sep 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=153215&lang=1&reg=3
  - **Claim summary:** The government highlighted expanded health coverage for seniors, U-WIN, more medical seats, and digital health registries. This is direct positive evidence for vulnerable-group access to basic health services, though it is official self-reporting.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2

- **Title:** Digital health infrastructure scaled up
  - **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
  - **Date:** 17 Dec 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2085201&lang=2&reg=48
  - **Claim summary:** ABDM reportedly built large-scale digital health infrastructure, including ABHA accounts and linked records. This supports a claim of broader access and continuity in health care for ordinary and vulnerable users.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2

- **Title:** Women’s SHG mobilization at massive scale
  - **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Rural Development
  - **Date:** 30 Jul 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2039162&lang=2&reg=48
  - **Claim summary:** The ministry said DAY-NRLM had mobilized more than 10 crore rural women into self-help groups. This is strong evidence of prioritizing poorer women and rural households through social protection and economic inclusion.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

- **Title:** PMAY-G and gendered housing ownership
  - **Publisher:** PTI via ThePrint
  - **Date:** 31 Dec 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/women-empowerment-remained-in-focus-for-rural-development-ministry-in-2024/2425889/
  - **Claim summary:** The ministry said over half of MGNREGS beneficiaries were women and PMAY-G housing strongly favored women’s ownership. This is direct evidence of prioritizing women and rural poor in housing and livelihood support.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2

- **Title:** PMAY-G adapted support for hill and northeast states
  - **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Rural Development
  - **Date:** 9 Aug 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2043919&lang=2&reg=48
  - **Claim summary:** The Cabinet extended PMAY-G with different unit assistance for hill and northeastern states. That is a real prioritization of poorer and higher-cost regions rather than a one-size-fits-all model.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2

- **Title:** Minority-women empowerment and skills
  - **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Minority Affairs
  - **Date:** 11 Dec 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2083334&lang=2&reg=48
  - **Claim summary:** The government said PM VIKAS/Nai Roshni trained about 4.35 lakh minority women and emphasized rights, literacy, and leadership. This is useful positive evidence for minority women and marginalized communities, though it is official self-reporting.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

- **Title:** Minority community scholarships and empowerment schemes continued
  - **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Minority Affairs
  - **Date:** 7 Aug 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2042759&lang=1&reg=3
  - **Claim summary:** The ministry listed scholarships and socio-economic empowerment schemes for the six centrally notified minority communities. This is direct evidence of targeted support to a vulnerable minority population.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2

- **Title:** Vulnerable-sections advisories covered SC/STs, women, children, and seniors
  - **Publisher:** Ministry of Home Affairs / Government of India
  - **Date:** 2 Jul 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.mha.gov.in/en/commoncontent/advisories-0
  - **Claim summary:** The Home Ministry listed advisories on protection of vulnerable sections, including women, children, senior citizens, and SC/ST communities. This supports the view that the state was at least formally attending to marginalized groups.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.1

- **Title:** Manipur relief package included food, medicine, and rehabilitation
  - **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs
  - **Date:** 17 Jun 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2025980&lang=2&reg=48
  - **Claim summary:** The ministry said it was committed to safety in Manipur and outlined support for food, water, medicine, health, education, and rehabilitation for displaced people. This is direct evidence of a vulnerable-populations response in a major crisis.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 3B.1

- **Title:** Pension and food support for the poorest elderly, widows, and disabled people
  - **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Government of India
  - **Date:** 2025-? [crawled yesterday in search result]
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210378&lang=1&reg=1
  - **Claim summary:** The scheme description shows old-age pension, widow pension, disability pension, and food-grain support for AAY households including widows, disabled persons, and elderly people with no assured means of subsistence. I am using this as structural evidence for the welfare architecture, but it is not a sharp 2024 performance claim.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2

- **Title:** Ex-servicemen and widows received welfare and rehabilitation support
  - **Publisher:** Ministry of Defence / PIB
  - **Date:** 2 Aug 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2040796&lang=2&reg=48
  - **Claim summary:** The ministry listed grants for elderly ex-servicemen, widows, disabled children, and widow remarriage and education support. This is evidence that the government did prioritize some vulnerable groups through formal welfare channels.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3

**Counterevidence**

- **Title:** Rural voters still cited jobs and inflation as unmet needs
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint
  - **Date:** 7 Jun 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/rural-vote-fall-cost-indias-modi-a-decisive-election-win/2121496/
  - **Claim summary:** Reuters reported that rural BJP losses were driven by jobs and inflation problems. This is strong evidence that many vulnerable households did not feel materially prioritized.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.10

- **Title:** Voter survey tied weaker support to prices, jobs, and falling incomes
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint
  - **Date:** 6 Jun 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/modis-appeal-clouded-in-india-election-by-prices-jobs-graft-survey-says/2119215/
  - **Claim summary:** The survey-based reporting links support erosion to household distress. That undercuts the claim that the government had clearly improved welfare for ordinary or vulnerable people.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.10

- **Title:** Food inflation cut school meal quality for poor children
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint
  - **Date:** 11 Oct 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-high-food-inflation-leaves-less-in-lunch-boxes-of-poor-school-children/2307077/
  - **Claim summary:** Reuters reported that school meal budgets had not kept pace with inflation, forcing cutbacks in nutrition for poor children. This is direct counterevidence on children’s welfare and food security.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.2

- **Title:** Manipur violence persisted with displacement and shutdowns
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch
  - **Date:** 11 Jan 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/india-increased-abuses-against-minorities-critics
  - **Claim summary:** HRW reported deaths, displacement, destroyed homes/churches, prolonged internet shutdowns, and detention of protesting women wrestlers. This is strong evidence that vulnerable groups were not reliably protected.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 3B.1

- **Title:** Amnesty said authorities failed to protect displaced residents in Manipur
  - **Publisher:** Amnesty International
  - **Date:** 16 Jul 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/india-authorities-missing-in-action-amid-ongoing-violence-and-impunity-in-manipur-state-new-testimonies/
  - **Claim summary:** Amnesty said the BJP-led state and central governments failed to end the violence, protect displaced residents, or hold vigilante groups accountable. This is direct counterevidence to a claim of strong protection for vulnerable communities.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 3B.1

- **Title:** Jammu and Kashmir repression continued
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch
  - **Date:** 31 Jul 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/31/india-repression-persists-jammu-and-kashmir
  - **Claim summary:** HRW reported arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killings, and little accountability. That weakens any broad claim that the government prioritized vulnerable populations in practice.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 3B.1

- **Title:** Campaign rhetoric stigmatized Muslims and minorities
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint
  - **Date:** 23 Apr 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-calls-rivals-pro-muslim-as-election-campaign-changes-tack/2053223/
  - **Claim summary:** Reuters reported Modi called Muslims “infiltrators” and linked them to wealth redistribution fears. That is counterevidence because it shows vulnerable minorities were also targets of political mobilization, not just beneficiaries of protection.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 6B.1, 2B.6

- **Title:** EC ordered BJP to stop communal campaigning
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint
  - **Date:** 22 May 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-poll-panel-orders-modis-bjp-opposition-congress-to-show-restraint-in-campaign/2096809/
  - **Claim summary:** The Election Commission told BJP campaigners to stop communal campaigning after complaints about divisive speech. That supports a reading that political messaging often ran against minority protection rather than in favor of it.
  - **Question IDs:** 6B.3, 2B.6

**Synthesis**
- **Best positive case:** Modi’s 2024 government did direct real resources toward women, rural poor, minorities, elderly, disabled people, and some vulnerable regional populations through budgets, pensions, housing, SHGs, scholarships, and health programs.
- **Best negative case:** those priorities were inconsistent in outcomes, and vulnerable groups still experienced food stress, rural distress, communal targeting, and serious violence/security failures.
- **Overall:** I would rate this **moderately positive on stated priority and program design, but mixed on actual protection and lived results**.
- **Search gap:** I found strong material on women, minorities, rural households, seniors, disabled people, and children, but **less direct independent evidence on water/sanitation outcomes** and fewer hard outcome measures for whether the schemes materially improved conditions across all vulnerable groups.
